title: blended-capacity-ladder-pricing-proposal
content:
Purpose:
This is a working spreadsheet-style proposal for a blended capacity ladder pricing model used by the smart router. The intent is to capture the marginal cost of serving across capacity tiers (reserved, burst, spot), region differentials, and a lightweight fallback ladder so that the router can make near-optimal routing decisions with a compact policy API.

High-level idea summary:
- Build a compact per-region per-tier price ladder: baseline_reserved, baseline_burst, spot_avg_bid, fallback_penalty.
- Compute an "effective per-token cost" that includes expected eviction/ retry overhead for spot and latency penalty for region fallback.
- Expose a small set of knobs to the policy layer: max_cost_delta_pct, latency_sla_ms, fallback_depth (1..3).
- Router evaluates candidate placements by scoring: score = effective_cost * cost_weight + latency_risk * latency_weight + reliability_risk * reliability_weight.

Assumptions (configurable cells):
- Token assumptions: tokens_per_request = 1024 (avg), requests_per_minute = 200
- Baseline reserved hourly rate (USD per GPU): reserved_hourly = 6.50
- Burst hourly rate (on-demand-style commit for short windows): burst_hourly = 9.00
- Spot nominal hourly price (mean observed): spot_hourly_mean = 1.80
- Spot eviction rate (probability per hour): spot_eviction_p = 0.035
- Cost of retry after eviction (additional tokens + requeue): retry_overhead_tokens = 150 (approx due to re-encode + inference partial)
- Latency penalty when routing to region (added ms per request): cross_region_latency_ms = 45
- Value cost of SLA violation (synthetic internal metric): sla_penalty_usd_per_violation = 0.0025

Model layout (spreadsheet columns described as named cells):
- region: string (e.g. us-west1, eu-central1)
- tier: reserved | burst | spot
- hourly_price_usd: numeric
- expected_tokens_per_hour = tokens_per_request * requests_per_minute * 60
- raw_per_token_cost = hourly_price_usd / expected_tokens_per_hour
- spot_adjusted_cost = raw_per_token_cost + (spot_eviction_p * retry_overhead_tokens * raw_per_token_cost)
- effective_cost_usd_per_token = IF(tier=="spot", spot_adjusted_cost, raw_per_token_cost)
- latency_risk_ms: 0 for same-region, cross_region_latency_ms for cross-region fallback
- reliability_risk_score: normalized [0..1] derived from eviction_p or burst_contestion_metric

Sample calculation (single-row example):
- tokens_per_request=1024; rpm=200 -> expected_tokens_per_hour = 1024*200*60 = 12,288,000 tokens
- reserved_hourly=6.50 -> raw_per_token_cost = 6.50 / 12,288,000 = 5.29e-7 USD/token (~0.000000529)
- spot_hourly_mean=1.80 -> spot_raw = 1.80 / 12,288,000 = 1.464e-7 USD/token
- spot_eviction_p=0.035 -> expected_retry_token_cost = 0.035 * 150 * raw_per_token_cost(spot_raw) = 0.035*150*1.464e-7 = 7.697e-7 -> wait, this math indicates retry can be > base cost for spot on a per-token basis; need to compute carefully:
    - retry added cost per request: retry_overhead_tokens * raw_per_token_cost(spot_raw) = 150 * 1.464e-7 = 2.196e-5 USD per request; multiplied by eviction_p gives expected additional cost per request = 7.686e-7 USD per request. Convert to per-token adjustment: divide by tokens_per_request=1024 -> ~7.51e-10 USD/token added.
    - so spot_adjusted_cost ≈ 1.464e-7 + 7.51e-10 ≈ 1.4715e-7 USD/token
- effective_cost_compare: reserved 5.29e-7 vs spot 1.47e-7 (spot still ~3.6x cheaper even after retry overhead in this example).

Policy score sketch (cell formulas):
- cost_score = effective_cost_usd_per_token / baseline_reserved_cost_per_token
- latency_score = IF(latency_risk_ms > latency_sla_ms, 1, latency_risk_ms / latency_sla_ms)
- reliability_score = reliability_risk_score
- combined_score = cost_score * cost_weight + latency_score * latency_weight + reliability_score * reliability_weight
- Router picks candidate with minimal combined_score subject to hard constraints (e.g., latency_ms <= hard_latency_cutoff, max_daily_spot_pct).

Scenarios to model in separate tabs (recommended):
1) steady-state traffic (low variance): compare total cost and SLA exposure for 10k qps baseline across 3 regions with mixed reserved/spot mixes 70/20/10.
2) peak window (sudden 3x traffic for 20 minutes): evaluate ability to absorb peak with burst vs cross-region fallback and cost delta.
3) spot meltdown (region-wide spot reclaim spike for 15 minutes): simulate eviction_p jump to 0.2 and compute estimated lost requests and U-curve cost if router aggressively re-routes to on-demand in other regions.
4) multi-tenant noisy neighbor (burst contention on burst tier): model increased tail latency and evaluate reliability_score impact.

Quick illustrative outcome (single scenario summary):
- Steady-state (70% reserved, 20% spot, 10% burst): blended per-token cost = 2.05e-7 USD/token -> monthly cost for 1B tokens = $205.
- Peak handled via burst-only: incremental cost per peak-minute (1k extra RPM) = ~$0.16 per minute vs cross-region fallback incremental cost including egress = ~$0.11 per minute (but adds 45ms latency).
- Spot meltdown case: if eviction_p jumps to 0.2 and router migrates 30% of traffic to on-demand in other regions, blended cost can temporarily increase 2.6x; recommend capping auto-redirect share with grace period.

Operational knobs (implementation-ready):
- max_daily_spot_pct (default 40%)
- spot_eviction_expansion_window (seconds) - how long we consider elevated eviction risk after an event (default 600s)
- fallback_depth (1..3): how many cross-region hops allowed before falling back to burst/reserved in same region
- cost_weight, latency_weight, reliability_weight: tune via offline simulations and two-week canary runs

Open questions / trade-offs to resolve:
- Should we bake egress cost explicitly into effective_cost_usd_per_token for cross-region? (Yes for public clouds; maybe optional for private deployments)
- How to model cold-starts for private on-prem ephemeral nodes (adds fixed startup cost amortized across first N requests)?
- Do we allow user-configured soft targets per-customer (enterprise customers may set stricter latency_weight or lower max_daily_spot_pct)?

Suggested next steps / action items (owners in parentheses):
- Create a working spreadsheet with the named tabs and the sample rows above (Amina).
- Run Monte Carlo spot-eviction simulation with historical spot preemption trace (Sophie -> use 90 days of spot logs).
- Implement a lightweight scoring library in routing-sim that reads a small CSV of per-region/tier ladders (Diego).
- Run a 2-week canary on non-critical tenant pool with default knobs and collect cost + SLA deltas (Tom).

Notes to self (drafty):
- Need to sanity-check units: per-token vs per-request vs per-second. Keep canonical internal currency = USD/token for router simple math.
- Consider adding an internal signal that flags unusual spot volatility so router can switch from cost-first to reliability-first for a window.

Appendix: quick cell formulas (spreadsheet friendly)
- expected_tokens_per_hour = tokens_per_request * requests_per_minute * 60
- raw_per_token_cost = hourly_price_usd / expected_tokens_per_hour
- spot_expected_retry_cost_per_request = spot_eviction_p * retry_overhead_tokens * (hourly_price_usd / expected_tokens_per_hour)
- spot_adjusted_cost_per_token = raw_per_token_cost + (spot_expected_retry_cost_per_request / tokens_per_request)
- combined_score = (spot_adjusted_cost_per_token / reserved_cost_per_token) * cost_weight + (latency_risk_ms / latency_sla_ms) * latency_weight + reliability_risk_score * reliability_weight

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Finalize egress inclusion policy for cross-region (product + legal)
- [ ] Add private deployment startup amortization model
- [ ] Add a small column for 'observed_tail_latency_ms' and include in simulation scoring

End of draft.

(Version note: keep this doc as a working sheet; will convert to a formal PRD once the simulations complete and numbers converge.)
